assessment.cross_component_synthesis: On March 24, the dominant behavioral pattern is a sustained and high rate of physical protective compliance coexisting with pronounced deterioration across nearly every functional domain. Residents across the country continue to enter shelters when sirens sound — and the evidence is direct: multiple incidents confirm that shelter use prevented casualties in Tel Aviv, Nesher, and Dimona — yet the same population is simultaneously experiencing school closures, near-cessation of commercial aviation, food price increases, and a 620% surge in crisis line calls within 48 hours of the current operation's onset. The gap between effective life-protective behavior and collapsing daily-life systems is widening. Leadership is producing frequent, visible public communication but simultaneously generating inconsistent operational guidance — particularly on education — creating a documented pattern of zigzagging directives that leaves parents and municipalities managing contradictions rather than receiving stable instructions. Community capital remains the most actively adaptive layer: 170 volunteers in the Golan, hundreds of municipal volunteers in Arad, a Yavne municipal shelter-sharing program, and civilian organizations launching emergency crowdfunding for farm shelters all point to a population that is compensating for institutional gaps through self-organization. However, belonging and solidarity are under pressure from visible internal tensions — including documented incidents of celebration during sirens and violent disturbances in Judea and Samaria — while the wellbeing of at-risk populations, particularly the 714,000 elderly and disabled unable to reach shelters, and the approximately one-third of the population lacking adequate shelter access, remains structurally unaddressed.
assessment.evidence_quality_note: Today's signal base is substantially larger than prior days (196 articles), with a high proportion of direct individual quotations alongside quantified institutional data, yielding medium-to-high confidence across most components; however, geographic dispersion remains uneven, with urban centers and named municipalities over-represented relative to peripheral and rural communities.

manifestations_evidenced: A narrative of successful coping is visible and circulating (residents/officials describe coping as effective)
Competing or contradictory narratives are explicitly voiced by residents or groups
manifestations_absent: The coping story reflects the entire population, not just a subset (informative absence)
Residents express that the authority's narrative is credible and reflects their lived reality (likely reporting gap)
evidence: Bar-Ilan policy researcher Anat Panti articulated a positive national coping frame: 'Social cohesion, community, level of trust among certain populations and sense of meaning explain Israel's high ranking. We are very high in generosity and social support' ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/theheadline/article/fcpbrey81))

Metula council head David Azulai expressed forward-looking confidence even during wartime: 'Even in the war, I'm happy about such news. There was crazy demand here,' describing plans for post-war recovery ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/economy/article/bype5occ11x))

Shaare Zedek nursing director Bat Ami Israel described institutional calm: 'When an alert sounds, the mothers and staff stay in place. No one needs to run anywhere. Even if we're in the middle of a cesarean, the service continues as usual and the alerts simply pass over us.' ([source](https://www.kikar.co.il/kikarfm/shaare-zedek-wartime-births-1))

Public figure Miriam Peretz voiced a collective continuity narrative: 'We are a people that does not lose hope. It is in our DNA... There will be a beautiful Seder. Maybe crowded, maybe with alerts - but full of life.' ([source](https://www.inn.co.il/news/692889))

A competing informational dynamic is documented: social media creates 'contagion chains where shares and reactions amplify same content repeatedly, creating spirals difficult to exit,' with many videos containing AI elements 'interpreted as truth in first minutes of exposure' ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/digital/internet/article/b11kw9c511e))

Nea Bardogo-Pasternak, director of a Jerusalem senior residence, framed community as a resilience mechanism: 'In moments of emergency, loneliness intensifies, and precisely then the importance of community sharpens. Our role is to enable residents to continue living and creating, even when reality outside is shaking.' ([source](https://www.kipa.co.il/%D7%94%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%95%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D/1221541-0/))
components.narrative: A visible and actively circulated coping narrative is present in today's sample, expressed by public figures, institutional leaders, and community directors — continuing the upward trend from prior days. Miriam Peretz's framing of national persistence ('a people that does not lose hope'), the Shaare Zedek nursing director's description of undisrupted surgical operations during alerts, and the Metula council head's forward orientation collectively constitute a coherent positive coping frame. However, this narrative is explicitly carried by named individuals and institutional spokespersons, and there is no direct evidence that it reflects the experience of the broader population, including evacuees, parents without childcare frameworks, or the approximately one-third of residents lacking adequate shelter access. A contradictory informational current runs alongside: documented social media rumor propagation — including AI-modified videos treated as factual in the first minutes of exposure — introduces competing interpretations of events that are difficult to correct once circulated. No evidence was found of residents explicitly evaluating whether authority communications reflect their lived reality, which represents a gap in the available signal base rather than confirmed absence.

manifestations_evidenced: Residents report information gaps, confusion, or spread of rumors/misinformation
Authority communication mechanisms are adapted to different resident groups (language, channel, format)
Residents express trust in information received from the authority
manifestations_absent: Residents state they receive the information they need to function during the emergency (informative absence)
Population perceives national media information as relevant and addressing their needs (likely reporting gap)
evidence: The Education Ministry cancelled in-person learning nationwide while simultaneously announcing Passover camps would open in requesting municipalities, generating documented confusion about the distinction between formal education and camp frameworks ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/b1qtkcc911e))

A repeated pattern is documented: 'Since war start, Education Ministry has zigzagged between guidelines, sending contradictory messages. Recently announced different decisions for limited school openings, then changed them due to missile hits. About 90 municipalities involved' ([source](https://www.haaretz.co.il/news/education/2026-03-23/ty-article/.premium/0000019d-16e5-de86-abff-97fd13bb0000))

Sirens were activated in Gush Dan and central Israel — including Bat Yam, Holon, and Rishon Lezion — without prior alerts in Home Front Command apps; initial warnings had been issued only for Lachish and the Judean Lowlands ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424419))

Bat Yam Mayor Tzvika Brot publicly clarified the discrepancy: 'The last siren was activated without prior warning due to concern about interceptor debris falling in our area'; Home Front Command then reiterated the 10-minute post-siren guidance ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424419))

Airport Authority CEO Sharon Kadmi communicated consistent institutional methodology: 'Risk management and performance assessment updated daily. Conditions forced us to make decisions that were not made hastily, weighed carefully' ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300425))

The US Embassy organized structured communication and logistical assistance for US citizens, including overland departure routes via Jordan and enrollment in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program for ongoing security alerts ([source](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-890962))

Social media contagion dynamics are documented as an active competing information channel: AI-modified videos are circulated and 'interpreted as truth in first minutes of exposure' ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/digital/internet/article/b11kw9c511e))

IDF officer provided direct public assurance on one category of threat: 'We can look residents in the eye and say that this threat, in a tangible sense, does not exist. There is no raid threat.' ([source](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/hjyoi00rqbe))
components.narrative: The most consistent finding in this component is a split between two parallel communication realities: protective-action guidance on shelter use and immediate threat response is structured, multi-channel, and reaches residents — while operational guidance on daily-life decisions, particularly education, has been inconsistent to the point of producing documented public confusion. The Education Ministry's successive contradictory directives, affecting approximately 90 municipalities, exemplify a pattern in which residents receive instructions that are then reversed or qualified without a stable framework replacing them. Alert system gaps compound this dynamic: sirens activated in central Israel without corresponding Home Front Command app notifications required municipal mayors to independently issue clarifying statements, placing local officials in a reactive correction role. Institutional leaders in other domains — airport operations, military — are communicating with measurable specificity, but this operational clarity has not extended to the systems affecting daily parental and civic decisions. No direct evidence was found of residents reporting satisfaction with the information they receive for non-protective daily functioning, which under current conditions of school closure and aviation disruption represents an informative absence.

manifestations_evidenced: Residents are observed or reported to actually follow Home Front Command (HFC) protective guidelines (sheltering, evacuating, etc.)
Residents demonstrate knowledge and understanding of HFC guidelines
Residents or officials report non-compliance with protective guidelines
Residents express or demonstrate perception of the situation as genuinely life-threatening
manifestations_absent: Community teams or roles actively promote emergency preparedness among residents (likely reporting gap)
evidence: Multiple independent incidents confirm shelter use prevented casualties: a Home Front Command official stated an Iranian warhead 'caused significant damage to three Tel Aviv buildings but resulted in only three light injuries because most residents took cover in nearby bomb shelter' ([source](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/home-front-command-official-iranian-warhead-badly-damaged-3-tel-aviv-buildings/))
In Nesher, a building sustained a direct cluster missile hit; no residents were injured because they had gone to the building's bomb shelter ([source](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/b1y5x8ki11l))

Resident Nadav Banshir described immediate shelter compliance: 'I heard the alert and then a huge boom. I went down to the shelter, that's my miracle' ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/rych4lyjbl))

A contrasting non-compliance pattern is documented at a population level: 'Most injured in the Arad incident simply did not bother to reach a protected space'; separately, a protected space in Etz Efraim was locked due to vandalism, forcing residents to run to distant locations during alerts ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/yokra14718859)) ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300045))

A transportation non-compliance pattern recurs: passengers exited buses to shelter during alerts, but buses departed before the Home Front Command all-clear, leaving passengers without transport — a repeated pattern across multiple reported incidents ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300127))

Nine foreign construction workers were arrested at a Yavne site for singing and dancing during alerts while residents ran to shelters; a resident reported: 'When we run to protected spaces, they sing and dance here, it's really scary' ([source](http://news.walla.co.il/item/3825672))

Aggregate outcome data confirm the compliance effect: 'Nearly all those who took shelter in building bomb shelters in Dimona were not hurt; majority of injured in Yavne were outside protected areas at time of impact' ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424444))

IDF instructed residents of Lebanon border communities and northern Golan Heights to remain near protected spaces, minimize movement, and avoid gatherings ([source](https://www.srugim.co.il/news/1300391))
components.narrative: Shelter compliance is the most behaviorally robust finding in today's dataset and continues an upward trend from prior days — with multiple incident-level confirmations that shelter use directly determined casualty outcomes in Tel Aviv, Nesher, and Dimona. Residents demonstrate both the knowledge and the behavioral disposition to enter protected spaces when alerts sound, and official outcome summaries explicitly attribute low casualty rates to this compliance. A meaningful non-compliance segment persists, however, and is documented across distinct population categories: residents in Arad who did not reach protected spaces, a foreign workforce that did not comply at a Yavne construction site, and bus operators who abandoned passengers mid-alert — each representing a different mechanism of non-compliance. The locked shelter in Etz Efraim introduces an infrastructure failure that converts compliant intent into exposure, regardless of individual behavior. The overall pattern is one of high compliance among the settled resident population combined with localized but consequential gaps at the margins — in migrant workers, infrastructure, and transport operations.

manifestations_evidenced: Schools and educational institutions are open and operating (or explicitly closed/disrupted)
Essential services (healthcare, supply chains, municipal services) continue to operate
Specific disruptions to daily life are reported (closures, evacuations, inability to work)
Residents report that sufficient resources are available to maintain routine functioning
manifestations_absent: Residents succeed in managing daily life (reported continuation of work, commerce, or social roles) (informative absence)
evidence: Education system closure costs the economy approximately 1.25 billion shekels per week; hundreds of thousands of parents are forced to remain home with children ([source](https://www.bhol.co.il/news/1722685))

Attorney and mother of four Hagar Gerty Zada described the situation: 'There are no frameworks. Simply none. We're dealing with children at home for long days with no real answer from system. Yes, Zoom isn't ideal, but at least gave children some framework, social meeting. Today there's not even that' ([source](http://news.walla.co.il/item/3825700))

Ben-Gurion Airport departing passenger volume dropped 85% since March 5; restrictions allow only 1–2 flights per hour with a maximum of 100 passengers per flight ([source](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/travel/2026-03-23/ty-article/tel-avivs-airport-restrictions-push-israelis-to-fly-via-sinai-and-jordan/0000019d-15b4-db4d-a5fd-5fb70f1e0000))

Arkia Airlines stated: 'the current framework does not allow for normal aviation activity and effectively constitutes a closure of Israel's skies' ([source](https://www.ynetnews.com/travel/article/bymghoc511x))

Lufthansa Group — including Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, and Brussels Airlines — suspended routes to Israel until at least May 31 ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/lifestyle/travel/article-1300253))
Events sector reported a 90% drop since the start of Operation Lion's Roar ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/economy/article/yokra14716620))

More than 3 million Israelis — approximately one-third of the population — lack adequate shelter protection; in 2025, more than half of Israeli apartments had no bomb shelter ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/living-architecture/local/Article-c9e597c6ebe1d91026.htm))

Healthcare services demonstrate a functional split: Shaare Zedek Medical Center relocated its maternity ward to a protected underground facility and is operating all obstetric services fully during alerts ([source](https://www.kikar.co.il/kikarfm/shaare-zedek-wartime-births-1)); the Bazan oil refinery restarted operations after interception fragment damage ([source](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/bazan-oil-refinery-says-all-activities-to-resume-in-haifa-in-coming-days-after-missile-attack-damage/))

Jerusalem Municipality opened pre-Passover camps for ages 3–6 and grades 1–3 in protected kindergartens; Golan Regional Council activated an emergency education system for ages birth through 9 with Ministry of Education budget support ([source](https://www.inn.co.il/news/692924)) ([source](https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001538231))

A father described a normalizing pattern under stress: 'There is normalization of war. The expectation is that whether or not there is an alert, you go to the meeting' ([source](https://www.haaretz.co.il/tmr/news/2026-03-24/ty-article-magazine/.premium/0000019d-1ab1-d8da-a7dd-fff57f5a0000))

Bank of Israel estimated a welfare loss of approximately 35,000 shekels per capita over nine quarters of fighting, with total fiscal war costs at 350 billion shekels, not including the current operation ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/finances-news/Article-fbb2b24962a1d91026.htm))
components.narrative: Functional continuity is the most disrupted component in today's assessment, maintaining the low score seen on March 23 and showing no directional improvement. The disruption is not uniform but patterned across sectors: healthcare services have adapted structurally — maternity wards relocated underground, critical industry restarted within days — while mass-participation systems, particularly education and aviation, have effectively ceased normal operation. Schools are closed nationwide following the Arad and Dimona strikes; aviation capacity is reduced by 85% in departing passenger volume, with multiple carriers describing current restrictions as equivalent to a full closure of Israeli skies. A coordination failure documented in the Etz Efraim protected space case — in which the council, Home Front Command, and police each referred responsibility to another body — illustrates a systemic gap in accountability for protective infrastructure maintenance. Some municipalities have produced workable partial alternatives, including Jerusalem's Passover camps and the Golan Regional Council's volunteer-staffed emergency education program, but these are locally generated responses to a nationally unresolved problem. Direct resident testimony confirms that the absence of childcare frameworks is the primary source of experienced dysfunction for working parents, while food price increases and supply chain pressure add cumulative economic stress to populations already managing without normal daily structures.

manifestations_evidenced: Residents volunteer or express willingness to volunteer in formal or informal frameworks
Authority or organizations are observed to activate and coordinate community resources
Mechanisms exist and operate to coordinate volunteers and community organizations
Cross-sector cooperation (e.g., municipality + NGOs + businesses) is reported or observed
evidence: In the Golan Regional Council, 170 volunteers — including 80% of the council's kindergarten teachers and 40 additional teachers — established an emergency education system for ages birth through 9, coordinated with the Ministry of Education and supported by a 150,000-shekel flexible budget allocation ([source](https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001538231))

In Arad, 291 evacuees were transferred to Dead Sea hotels; the municipality opened an enhanced aid center employing hundreds of volunteers and receiving large-scale donations; 40 Amidar apartments are being repaired for evacuee housing ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300131))

Yavne municipality distributed hundreds of signs to homes and buildings reading 'Welcome to enter protected space in this house during alert,' expanding the available shelter network through a structured municipal-civilian initiative ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/breaking-news/article-1300203))

Hashomer Hachadash launched an emergency crowdfunding campaign in partnership with the Harvey and Gloria Kaylie Foundation, targeting placement of 60–120 bomb shelters on farms to protect agricultural workers currently operating in exposed fields ([source](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-890925))

Israel Hotels Association mobilized 116 hotels nationwide in the 'To the North with a Benefit' initiative, offering northern residents a free third night as a cross-sector business-community response ([source](https://www.jpost.com/consumerism/article-890750))

Finance Ministry and Labor Ministry agreed on a special aid framework including refunds to parents for days without childcare activity, advances to caregivers, and guarantees of rapid daycare resumption ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/politics/article-1299975))

Gan Dvora kindergarten in Nesher, on learning a child was not eating at home, arranged for staff to deliver food from the kindergarten to the child's home in the evening ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-kids/Article-dc834351a361d91027.htm))

A coordination failure was also documented: residents seeking accountability for a locked shelter in Etz Efraim were redirected between the council, Home Front Command, and police without resolution ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300045))

Elderly residents in protected housing continued organized volunteering activities, including support for lone soldiers, during active operations ([source](https://www.kipa.co.il/%D7%94%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%95%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D/1221541-0/))
components.narrative: Community capital is today's most clearly improving component, scoring 8/10 and exhibiting evidence across all four expected behavioral manifestations. The range of documented activity spans individual informal acts — a kindergarten delivering food to a child who had stopped eating — to structured institutional initiatives involving 170 volunteers, inter-ministerial agreements, 116-hotel coalitions, and emergency crowdfunding campaigns with named philanthropic partners. A meaningful pattern in today's data is that community capital is functioning as a compensatory layer: where state systems have gaps — in agricultural shelter coverage, childcare frameworks, evacuee housing, and expanded shelter access — NGOs, municipalities, and voluntary associations are generating partial solutions. Cross-sector coordination is documented across at least four distinct modalities: municipality-civic (Yavne's shelter-sign program), government-business (hotels-north initiative), NGO-philanthropy (Hashomer Hachadash shelters), and inter-ministry (Finance-Labor aid framework). The one documented coordination failure — the Etz Efraim locked shelter — illustrates that even in a high-capital environment, inter-agency accountability gaps can produce outcomes that directly expose residents to risk.

Leadership is reported to function professionally and manage the situation competently
Residents express distrust, criticism, or frustration with leadership

President Isaac Herzog visited Kiryat Shmona and the Galilee, entering a shelter and receiving briefings from local officials ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424442))

President Herzog stated publicly: 'It is clear that the entire people of Israel are one united front, and the entire State of Israel stands in this campaign — this is a just campaign' ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424442))

Bat Yam Mayor Tzvika Brot proactively clarified the alert gap for residents: 'The last siren was activated without prior warning due to concern about interceptor debris falling in our area,' stepping into a communication gap left by the national system ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424419))

Yavne Mayor Roy Gavai publicly endorsed and framed the community shelter-sharing initiative: 'Here is real strength of our residents. There is warm community... I call on all who can open door in emergency to help us expand city security network' ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/breaking-news/article-1300203))

Education Minister Yoav Kish articulated a rationale for school closure: 'Decision not to open in routine is not to allow release of large masses of children at once on way to and from frameworks. In non-formal activity like camps there are fewer children' ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/education/article-1299847))

A documented pattern of inconsistency undermines that rationale: the Education Ministry has 'zigzagged between guidelines, sending contradictory messages' since the war's start, with approximately 90 municipalities affected by successive reversals ([source](https://www.haaretz.co.il/news/education/2026-03-23/ty-article/.premium/0000019d-16e5-de86-abff-97fd13bb0000))

An inter-agency accountability failure was documented in Etz Efraim: residents were redirected between four separate bodies — council, CEO, Home Front Command, and police — without any body accepting responsibility for the locked shelter ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300045))
components.narrative: Leadership functions across two distinct registers today, and the split between them is the analytically central finding for this component. Municipal and institutional leaders — airport operations, local mayors, medical system directors — are demonstrating structured decision-making, physical presence, and proactive public communication, including several cases where municipal leaders corrected gaps in national alert systems. At the national policy level, however, the Education Ministry's documentation as a source of 'zigzagging' and contradictory guidelines over the course of the war constitutes a sustained credibility problem that is distinguishable from today's operational decisions. The inter-agency failure in Etz Efraim, where no body accepted accountability for a locked shelter, reflects a structural leadership coordination gap that local responsiveness cannot compensate for. Presidential and military leadership are producing symbolic unity framing and direct public assurances on specific threats — the IDF officer's statement that ground raid threats do not exist, President Herzog's shelter visit — which address the psychological dimension of leadership visibility. No direct evidence was found of residents affirmatively characterizing leadership as a source of security or support, a gap likely attributable to reporting focus rather than confirmed public sentiment.

manifestations_evidenced: Concrete acts of mutual aid between residents are reported (helping neighbors, sharing resources, organizing support)
Population groups are reported as scapegoated, blamed, or excluded due to the emergency (negative signal)
Programs or events strengthening belonging are activated and attended
manifestations_absent: Residents express a sense of solidarity or shared fate (in their own words) (informative absence)
evidence: Yavne municipality distributed hundreds of signs to homes and buildings: 'Welcome to enter protected space in this house during alert,' operationalizing a norm of mutual shelter access at city scale ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/breaking-news/article-1300203))

Gan Dvora kindergarten arranged unsolicited food delivery to a child who had stopped eating at home — an informal solidarity act outside any formal mandate ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-kids/Article-dc834351a361d91027.htm))

Elderly residents in protected housing continued organized support for lone soldiers during active operations, maintaining a solidarity function under constrained conditions ([source](https://www.kipa.co.il/%D7%94%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%95%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D/1221541-0/))

The shelter-sharing dynamic is producing new social formations: 'mamadiyut' (shelter-mates) describes a structure in which previously distant neighbors share intimate moments of anxiety, creating forced proximity that functions as involuntary community-building ([source](https://www.ynet.co.il/laisha/article/byuhlhy911e))

Nine workers from Samaria were arrested for celebrating and cheering during sirens at a Yavne construction site; separately, IDF and Israel Police reported violent assaults, arson, and disturbances by Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria, with five civilians apprehended and one Border Police soldier injured ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/424415)) ([source](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/flashes/680705))

Elderly residents in protected housing are experiencing prolonged shelter stays, fear of leaving public spaces, and forced social disconnection — described as generating anxiety and psychological distress ([source](https://www.kipa.co.il/%D7%94%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%95%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D/1221541-0/))
components.narrative: Belonging and solidarity present a mixed behavioral picture today, declining from the previous day's score and reflecting two contradictory social dynamics operating simultaneously. Mutual aid is concrete and documented: the Yavne municipal shelter-sign program represents a deliberate institutionalization of neighbor-to-neighbor solidarity, while the kindergarten food delivery and lone-soldier support by elderly residents in protected housing reflect informal solidarity operating below organizational thresholds. The forced social proximity of shelter-sharing — described as 'mamadiyut' — is generating unexpected community formation between previously unacquainted neighbors, functioning as an unplanned belonging mechanism. Against this, incidents of public celebration during sirens and documented acts of violence in Judea and Samaria introduce visible internal tensions that qualify the solidarity picture. The incidents involving construction workers celebrating during rocket alerts generated public fear responses ('it's really scary'), indicating that these events affect the perceived social environment beyond the immediate actors. No direct first-person expressions of solidarity or shared fate were found in the sample — residents describe acts of mutual aid but do not explicitly frame them in solidarity terms — which may reflect the reporting sample's focus on events rather than affect.

manifestations_evidenced: Emotional support responses (psychological first aid, mental health services) are available and used by residents showing anxiety or trauma
Specific responses for at-risk or special-needs populations are reported as active (elderly, disabled, evacuees, etc.)
Reports of unmet mental health or physical wellbeing needs among residents
Residents in the second or third circle of vulnerability (indirectly affected) receive responses to their needs
evidence: Within 48 hours of Operation Lion's Roar beginning, calls to the Natal crisis line increased by 620%; Ido, 34, from Tel Aviv described accumulated impact: 'I haven't been in my routine for two and a half years. I'm not the same person. I'm treated with Cipralex to reduce anxiety and depression, and I know I depend on it. Once I was person of big dreams, today all that interests me is how I finish the day' ([source](http://news.walla.co.il/item/3825795))

Over-the-counter sleep and anxiety medication demand increased by 30%; prescription medications for the same conditions increased by 15%; a customer service representative described 'many calls from exhausted parents worried about children or themselves... chronic stress affecting many body systems, including sleep' ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/health/article-1300282))

714,000 elderly and disabled people cannot reach protected spaces during alerts; Lilach Michal-Shemesh, 48, from Holon stated: 'I'm not asking for luxuries — I'm asking to survive. I need a place where I can raise my daughter' ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-relationship/Article-d98e049403a1d91026.htm))

Wolfson Medical Center documented a 30% increase in fibromyalgia patient visits since the war began, with staff estimating that a further wave of exacerbations is expected ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/health-news/Article-5498ff4af650d91026.htm))

Soroka Medical Center continues to treat 24 wounded from the Dimona and Arad strikes, including 5 children and 1 adult in serious condition; medical staff were described as shocked by the volume and severity of child casualties ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/health-news/Article-6d7edf98e3a1d91027.htm))

Health Ministry reported 153 injured people transported to hospitals in the past 24 hours; 8 were treated specifically for anxiety ([source](https://www.kikar.co.il/arab-news/mda-casualties-operation-lions-roar-summary))

From October 2023 to end of 2024, 217 suspected suicides were recorded — below the pre-war annual average of 242. Experts warn this 'relative quiet' period typically precedes a delayed wave, as social cohesion weakens post-crisis ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1299724))

A parent described sustained sleep deprivation across multiple nights: 'My sleep was light to the point of ridicule. I didn't really fall asleep — just closed eyes between alerts. Here it's already become really hard. Accumulated fatigue showed its signs, nervousness was very noticeable in lack of patience' ([source](https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-relationship/Article-66db7069c891d91027.htm))

Arad evacuees — 291 in number — were housed in Dead Sea hotels with volunteer-staffed aid center support; this represents an active institutional response to a displaced population ([source](https://www.maariv.co.il/news/israel/article-1300131))

components.narrative: The wellbeing component carries the largest signal volume in today's sample and presents consistent evidence of population-level distress across multiple independent measurement channels. The 620% increase in crisis line calls, 30% increase in sleep and anxiety medication demand, and 30% increase in fibromyalgia clinic visits are quantified institutional indicators that converge with direct individual testimony — a resident describing 2.5 years of disrupted routine and pharmacological dependence, a parent unable to sleep between alerts, a mother unable to hold her hospitalized newborn during active conflict. The component's most structurally significant finding is the documented gap in provision for the 714,000 elderly and disabled individuals who cannot physically reach protected spaces: this population is described as dependent on private organizations rather than state systems, constituting an unmet need at a scale that private volunteerism cannot fully address. Response mechanisms are active — the Natal crisis line is operational, evacuees from Arad are receiving accommodation and volunteer support, and medical facilities are functioning — but they are absorbing demand that reflects ongoing inadequacy of prevention rather than recovery. The expert observation that suicide rates may increase months after the acute crisis phase, when social cohesion weakens, introduces a temporal dimension: current welfare losses may be measurably smaller than the delayed wave anticipated by mental health professionals.
